items.statement: A structured bedside handoff checklist with a four-line medicines section will reduce the weekly proportion of handoffs with at least one missed reconciliation item on Ward 6B from about 38 percent to 20 percent or less within 12 weeks.
items.rationale: Need is high given two near misses and a 38 percent baseline; novelty is low because similar tools exist, which suits local improvement; feasibility and parsimony are high because the change uses existing huddles and sheets.
items.risks: Checklist fatigue on nights, completion falling after the project, and reviewer bias in sheet review.

items.statement: Adding a pharmacy-pending line to the checklist will reduce missed items more than the medicines prompt alone.
items.rationale: Items awaiting pharmacist review are a plausible source of misses, but separating their effect needs more cycles than the ward can run this autumn.
items.risks: Adds length to the checklist and depends on pharmacy documentation that is not always current.

items.statement: Using the checklist at the 19:00 handoff only will achieve most of the reduction with half the workload.
items.rationale: Both near misses crossed the day-to-night change, but the local check found misses on both handoffs.
items.risks: Leaves the 07:00 handoff unimproved and complicates the run chart.

summary: Three hypotheses ranked; h1 selected as the simplest test of the full checklist.
